key_insight: BSPDN already forces a face-to-face bonded wafer onto every leading-edge logic die; making it DRAM gives ~45 GB at ~0.3 pJ/bit with no TSVs, PHYs or interposer.
killer_doubt: All logic heat (~125 W/cm2, hotspots ~1 kW/cm2) crosses the DRAM: Si cells at 95-105 C need ~16-32 ms refresh, and W2W compound yield scraps ~10% of good logic.
decisive_experiment: Hybrid-bond finished DRAM wafers face-down onto a dummy logic wafer with SiGe etch stop, thin to <1 um, run 400 C backside metal; map retention tail, bond-pad yield and overlay distortion before and after.
prior_art: imec proposed face-to-face memory-on-logic in a BSPDN stack (via search snippet); UniIC SeDRAM W2W hybrid-bonded DRAM-on-logic; Graphcore Bow power-carrier wafer.

key_insight: A latch is already a bifurcation amplifier; calibrating each amp's trip point is offset cancellation, which is the real lever for sub-fF sensing.
killer_doubt: Hopf gain amplifies noise equally, so SNR stays input-referred: 1 fF on a 35 fF bitline gives ~14 mV against ~10-20 mV SA offset; the poise drifts with temperature.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 28 nm MPW: compare a Hopf-poised amp with an offset-cancelled latch on identical 1 fF/35 fF bitlines; measure BER at 85 C and energy per sense. Drop unless Hopf wins >2x.
prior_art: Offset-cancellation sense amps in production DRAM; Hopf-bifurcation hearing models (Hudspeth, Magnasco); charge-transfer pre-sense (Phase B N-04) does this better.

key_insight: Retention failures are directional (charged to discharged), so true/anti-cell-aware low-weight coding shrinks the vulnerable population at near-zero circuit cost.
killer_doubt: With a retention-tail slope of ~3-5 on log-log, cutting charged cells 35% stretches refresh only ~1.08-1.15x, not 1.5x, while 16b-to-18b costs 12.5% capacity. VRT cells are unaffected.
decisive_experiment: On DRAM Bender with 20 DDR4/DDR5 chips, map true/anti cells, write low-weight versus random data, and sweep refresh from 64 ms to 4 s at 85 C; compare failing-bit counts and VRT share. ~$30k.
prior_art: Liu et al. ISCA 2013 data-dependent retention; bus-invert coding (Stan and Burleson 1995); value-aware refresh-skipping proposals.

key_insight: Clean file-backed data has a free backup, so a weak tier needs only detection; Linux already drops and re-reads clean page-cache pages on an uncorrectable error.
killer_doubt: In VM clouds the host sees guest page cache as anonymous, dirty memory. Clean, host-visible pages may be only ~10-20% of DRAM, capping savings at a few percent.
decisive_experiment: Measure host-visible clean-page residency on 1,000 container and VM hosts, then run a CXL tier of second-life DIMMs with CRC detection and 4x relaxed refresh under Linux tiering; count refetches and p99 latency.
prior_art: Luo et al. DSN 2014 heterogeneous-reliability memory (parity plus recovery of clean pages from disk); Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); Linux memory_failure clean-page recovery.

key_insight: Liquid-cooled AI racks hold DIMMs 50-60 C below spec. Retention roughly doubles per ~10 C, so a cold-certified grade has ~30x headroom for a 4-8x refresh stretch.
killer_doubt: Tail cells are GIDL or trap-assisted, with weak temperature activation and VRT. An 8x longer window lets ~5.3M activations hit a row versus ~0.7M. Rescued dies may be <2%.
decisive_experiment: Profile 500 DDR5 dies, including hot-retention rejects, on DRAM Bender at 30, 50 and 85 C; extract tail activation energy, VRT rate and hammer threshold at 256 ms; compute cold-grade yield. ~$100k.
prior_art: LPDDR temperature-compensated refresh via MR4; RAIDR (ISCA 2012) and AVATAR multi-rate refresh; vendor ETT/downgrade die sales.

key_insight: Identical data-parallel replicas are a free majority-vote copy, and checksumming 2 MB shards costs negligible bandwidth while catching silent data corruption.
killer_doubt: In mixed-precision Adam, bf16 weights are ~2 of ~16 bytes/param, and ZeRO shards the rest. One flipped weight pollutes gradients all-reduced to every replica within a step.
decisive_experiment: Inject bit flips into weight HBM in a 64-GPU DDP job and measure steps until cross-replica checksums diverge versus loss corruption. Then test read-only inference replicas, where weights dominate HBM.
prior_art: Fleet silent-data-corruption studies (Meta, Google); ABFT checksums; parameter-hash checks across DP replicas in Megatron-LM.

key_insight: Every chip in a rank sees identical activations. Mixing vendors with different hammer thresholds and layouts turns simultaneous multi-chip flips into single-symbol errors that chipkill corrects.
killer_doubt: Mixed ranks run at the slowest timings and the weakest refresh/PRAC behavior. If UEs are mostly single-device and channel faults, decorrelation buys <10% UE reduction.
decisive_experiment: Build homogeneous and three-vendor DDR5 RDIMM ranks on an FPGA controller; run hammer, retention and data-pattern stress at 85 C; compare multi-symbol errors per codeword. ~$150k.
prior_art: Dissimilar redundancy in avionics fly-by-wire; chipkill/SDDC; no memory application found.

key_insight: Cross-die sparing in stacks or ranks can rescue dies that exceed their own redundancy, if the controller remaps a bad row to a partner's good row.
killer_doubt: Random pairing already gives near-zero overlap: 100 bad rows each among ~2M rows gives ~0.005 expected collisions. Matching adds nothing; lockstep remap logic is the real cost, rescuing ~1-3%.
decisive_experiment: None separate: a Monte Carlo on vendor fail-bit maps (~$20k) shows random pairing suffices. The remap test belongs with host-level row retirement (I-06365).
prior_art: Selective assembly in bearing manufacture; DDR5 PPR/sPPR; ArchShield fault-map remapping (ISCA 2013).

key_insight: Retired DDR4/DDR5 is existing silicon needing zero fab capital. Deep retention/hammer profiling plus SPD weak-row maps behind CXL ECC turns scrap into a graded capacity tier.
killer_doubt: CXL adds ~70-170 ns, and DDR4-capable CXL controllers set the cost. If test plus controller exceeds ~$3-5/GB or the pass rate is <70%, it loses to new DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Profile 5,000 retired server DIMMs on an automated rack (retention to 4 s at 85 C, hammer, VRT); write weak-row maps to SPD; run 200 in a CXL tier for 6 months logging CE/UE. ~$400k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (reused DDR4 behind CXL, ISCA 2024); Pond CXL pooling; ITAD used-server-RAM resellers.

key_insight: Same core as I-00845. It adds tiered grading and elastic refresh for cold pools, which fits the clean-page weak tier (I-01324).
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00845. Usable supply is the annual retirement flow (~1/5-1/6 of the installed base at 5-6 year server lives), not the whole installed base.
decisive_experiment: None separate: settled by I-00845's 5,000-DIMM profiling and CXL field pilot.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU DDR4 reuse; ITAD resellers; same as I-00845.

key_insight: A signed per-die error map lets controllers retire rows and set refresh per bank, turning JEDEC rejects into predictable capacity instead of untested gray-market parts.
killer_doubt: ETT/UTT downgrade markets already absorb most of the 5-15% fallout. The map adds value only if controllers honor it, and DDR5 lacks per-bank refresh-rate control.
decisive_experiment: With one OSAT, map 2,000 rejected dies (retention, hammer, VRT over 7 days), load the maps into an FPGA DDR5/CXL controller, and verify zero UEs over 3 months versus unmapped controls. ~$300k.
prior_art: ETT/UTT downgrade die sales; ArchShield fault maps (ISCA 2013); RAIDR multi-rate refresh; DDR5 PPR.

key_insight: Corrected errors are free sensors of weak or hammered rows, and DDR5 DRFM can refresh an aggressor's victims on command, so a firmware-only response is feasible.
killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die SEC hides single-bit flips and patrol scrub takes ~24 h per pass, while hammer flips occur within one 32 ms window. Host CEs come too few, too late.
decisive_experiment: Replay published hammer and retention patterns on DRAM Bender with on-die ECC enabled; measure the fraction of rows where a host-visible CE precedes any UE within 32 ms. If <10%, stop.
prior_art: rasdaemon/mcelog CE-threshold page offlining; Meza et al. DSN 2015 page retirement; DDR5 ECS and DRFM; Intel ADDDC.
